vulnerablePath: Anyone holding a session cookie of their own
edit the token payload so that sub names another user
GET /api/orders calls supabase.auth.getSession(), which reads the cookie without revalidating it
the query runs with the service-role key, so Row Level Security never sees the forged token
the filter is scoped to the forged user_id and returns that user's orders
expectedSecureBehavior: The server establishes the caller with getUser() (asks the Auth server) or getClaims() (verifies the token signature), so an edited token is rejected before any query runs; genuine sessions keep working.
acceptableFixes: Replace getSession() with getUser() and take the id from the returned user
Replace getSession() with getClaims() and take the id from the verified claims
Read through the caller's own cookie client so Row Level Security checks the token
unacceptableFixes: Keeping getSession() and adding a second check that also reads the same cookie
Moving the identity filter into the client
Disabling Row Level Security so the difference stops showing
